 Janine Gutierrez’s toughest role wasn’t in front of the camera
 ‘I get motion sickness pretty easily, so it was one of the most challenging shoots for me.’
 Jefferson Fernando · 21 November 2026 · 12:34 AM PHT · 2 MIN READ 
 JANINE Gutierrez says filming aboard a boat for two days despite her motion sickness became the most challenging part of making ‘Balaraw: Blood Island.’
 Photograph courtesy of netflix
 Text size A− Reset A+ Save For Janine Gutierrez, the toughest part of filming Balaraw: Blood Island was spending two days aboard a boat in the middle of the sea.
 Although the production had safety personnel and freedivers on standby during the underwater scenes, Gutierrez — who is prone to motion sickness — said the experience pushed her to her limits.
 “I think the hardest part was filming on a boat way out at sea. We shot for two days. I get motion sickness pretty easily, so it was one of the most challenging shoots for me,” she recalled.

 SHOW Janine Gutierrez points to the emotional core of ‘Balaraw’
 Actress reveals why the emotional core of Netflix’s new Filipino thriller made her say yes.
 Pauline Songco · 17 October 2026 
 Seeing the finished series, however, made the experience worthwhile.
 “When I finally watched it, I was blown away. It was such a thrill to see that we’d actually pulled it off. So please watch it on Netflix,” she said.
 Gutierrez also reflected on how easily time slips by when she is immersed in work.
 “Sometimes five days go by and you ask yourself, ‘What have I actually done?’ That’s how I’ve felt these past few weeks. Sometimes you forget how much you’ve already done,” she said.
 A recent post on X also reminded her of the impact of her work. The post praised a scene from her other series, Loyalty Game, in which her character, Anna, sits inside a vehicle while Ben and Beth are reflected in the rearview mirror.
 Gutierrez said she was grateful that viewers noticed the details of her performance.
 “When people notice something I did in a scene and respond to it positively, it really makes me happy,” she said. “They saw the effort I put in, and the scene moved them. I’m so grateful for moments like that.”
 Directed by Rae Red, Balaraw: Blood Island premiered on 29 October. The Filipino mystery thriller follows Sabina as she searches for her missing mother, Rebecca, on an island steeped in local folklore, where she uncovers family secrets and encounters supernatural forces.
